7 انبعق It came upon one suddenly, unexpectedly, without his knowledge. (S, K, TA.) ―
-b2- انبعق المُزْنُ (tropical:) [The clouds, or white clouds, or clouds containing water,] clave asunder, with, or by reason of, rain, or violent rain; syn. اِنْبَعَجَ بِالمَطَرِ; (S, K, TA;) or opened vehemently with rain; (Z, TA;) and ↓ تبعّق signifies the same. (S.) ―
-b3- انبعق فُلَانٌ بِالجُودِ وَ الكَرَمِ (tropical:) [Such a one was profuse in bounty and generosity]. (TA.) ―
-b4- انبعق فِى الكَلَامِ (S, K) (assumed tropical:) He was profuse in speech; (K, * TA;) as also ↓ تبعّق (K) and ↓ ابتعق . (Sgh, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
